timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Why is Sentinel called cloud-native? What makes it different?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It runs entirely in Azure. No hardware to maintain, scales on demand, pay for what you ingest.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Microsoft 365, Azure services, AWS, GCP, syslog, CEF, and hundreds of third-party connectors.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Scheduled rules run KQL queries on intervals. Fusion rules use ML to correlate multiple low-confidence signals.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It correlates related alerts into a single high-fidelity incident. Detects multi-stage attacks.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Visual dashboards showing trends, metrics, and investigation views across your security data.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do I control who sees what in Sentinel?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: RBAC at the workspace level. Restrict access to specific tables, actions, or data ranges.
